claim_being_audited: The actor claims the current release can be certified now because aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, despite a current fraud-dispute subgroup regression, on the theory that current documentation and monitoring are sufficient under policy.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current-release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if material segment weaknesses are disclosed before launch or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness clearance and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient if the disclosure/mitigation predicate is unmet.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but do not satisfy current-release policy requirements.
evidence_requests: Provide the current model-card or release documentation showing the fraud dispute review regression is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation documentation tied to this current release and this subgroup weakness.
Provide the materiality determination showing why this subgroup weakness is or is not considered a material limitation under release policy.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current-release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation before certification.
Admissible evidence shows a current subgroup weakness: the fraud dispute review slice is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold.
Admissible evidence shows only an informal post-launch monitoring comment, with no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language attached.
Prior approval is expressly stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant now under the stated policy threshold.
That informal manual monitoring is an adequate substitute for approved mitigation or documented disclosure.
That the current release documentation already reflects the subgroup regression in the way policy requires.
